items.title: Challenges and the Repositioning of Islamic Religious Education Teachers in the Era of Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Perspective from Islamic Epistemology
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is reshaping how students access, produce, verify, and communicate information, raising questions about source authority, adab, values, and character formation in Islamic Religious Education (IRE). This study examines the challenges facing IRE teachers and proposes a repositioning of their roles from an Islamic epistemological perspective. A qualitative library research approach was employed, drawing on literature on Islamic education and epistemology, teacher ethics, UNESCO guidance on AI in education, and recent studies on AI and IRE. Sources were examined through content and conceptual analysis. The findings position AI as a supporting instrument subject to human epistemic oversight and identify teachers’ roles as knowledge curators, information validators, digital ethics mentors, learning designers, and exemplars of adab. AI outputs should be evaluated within the relationship among revelation, reason, experience, scholarly tradition, and technology. The study proposes the IRE teacher as an epistemic gatekeeper responsible for safeguarding information quality, guiding verification, and aligning technology use with Islamic educational aims. To support implementation, it introduces the Verifikasi model, comprising source verification, ethical use, reflection, integration of religious evidence, process orientation, human initiative, and accountability. The study contributes a conceptual basis and an implementation model for repositioning IRE teachers, emphasizing that AI integration should strengthen literacy, critical reasoning, and adab while preserving human responsibility in education.

items.title: Chance-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning
items.abstract: We study personalized LLM routing, where a router selects among heterogeneous models with different costs and capabilities. The router must minimize cumulative inference cost while ensuring reliable realized response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned from feedback during deployment. We formulate this problem as a constrained contextual bandit and develop an algorithm that learns preferences while balancing cost and quality. Under a logistic preference model and a strict-feasibility condition, we establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized contextual oracle and a high-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction. The framework extends beyond LLM routing to broader online model-selection problems with reliability requirements.

items.title: Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM-Based Text Scoring
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in computational social science to assign scalar scores to social and psychological constructs. However, studies use different rating scales, and whether their scores remain comparable across scale designs is understudied. To address this gap, we define and systematically investigate scale sensitivity, the variation in LLM-generated scores caused by rating scale design. We distinguish numerical sensitivity, changes in normalized scores, from semantic sensitivity, changes in score interpretation. To assess both, our experimental design crosses 2 formats (continuous vs. ordinal), 4 ranges (3, 5, 11, and 21 points), and 2 signs (signed vs. unsigned) across 3 tasks (political leaning, sentiment, and toxicity), 2 prompting strategies (zero-shot and rubric-based), and 5 LLMs. We find that changing one design element shifts normalized scores by about 0.10 on average and changes the category of roughly 20% of texts. Sensitivity is greatest for toxicity, the only unipolar construct examined. Also, rubric-based prompting does not reduce sensitivity compared with zero-shot prompting. We provide practical guidance for designing more reliable LLM-based text scoring and highlight the need for robustness checks across alternative scales.

items.title: Changes in functional outcomes following activity management training in individuals with chronic low back pain: associations with cognitive functions, body awareness, and fatigue
items.abstract: This study investigated changes in activity patterns, cognitive functions, and fatigue following activity management training in individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP). Thirty-four individuals with CLBP completed a six-week training program covering ergonomics, pacing, energy conservation, and relaxation. Assessments included the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), Body Awareness Questionnaire, Patterns of Activity Measure-Pain, Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), Fatigue Severity Scale, Stroop Test, and selected Loewenstein Occupational Therapy Cognitive Assessment (LOTCA) subtests. Significant improvements were observed in COPM performance and satisfaction (p < 0.001). Body awareness and adaptive activity regulation behaviors increased, while pain-related avoidance behaviors decreased (p < 0.05). Cognitive performance also improved, as indicated by lower CFQ scores and better performance on selected Stroop and LOTCA measures (p < 0.05). Fatigue severity did not change significantly (p > 0.05). Regression models were significant for activity performance (R2 = 0.366, p = 0.008) and satisfaction (R2 = 0.347, p = 0.013). Body awareness and visuomotor organization were associated with activity performance, while fatigue was associated with activity satisfaction (p < 0.05). Activity management training may be considered a supportive approach for addressing activity-related difficulties in individuals with chronic low back pain. www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07061743. For people with chronic low back pain, carrying out daily activities can be difficult. In particular, difficulties with activities such as walking, exercising, preparing meals, and doing household chores can make it harder for a person to maintain their usual daily routine. This study examined whether activity management training could help people with chronic low back pain manage the activities they have difficulty with in their daily lives. Thirty-four adults with chronic low back pain participated in a six-week activity management training program. The program addressed methods for protecting the body while performing activities, planning activities, and helping individuals use less energy and experience less fatigue. Participants attended a total of 12 sessions, twice a week. After the six-week program, participants reported improvements in their performance of daily activities and in their satisfaction with performing these activities. Positive changes were also observed in how participants performed their activities, their body awareness, and some cognitive skills. These findings suggest that activity management training may be an approach that can help people with chronic low back pain manage their daily activities. However, because the study did not include a comparison group and the number of participants was relatively small, larger studies using comparison groups and longer follow-up periods are needed to better evaluate the effects of activity management training.

items.title: Charting the Trajectory of Artificial Intelligence Agents in Air Traffic Control
items.abstract: The aim of the study was to chart the evolution and the current research landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) agents within the domain of air traffic control. Using bibliometric analysis, the study identified major research trends and gaps and provided a consolidated reference for researchers. The analysis included 58 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The findings showed that the earliest publication in the dataset appeared in 1998 and that research output increased noticeably after 2022. Publication output peaked in 2025, with 16 articles, indicating growing scholarly interest in AI agents for air traffic control. Citation analysis identified Agogino and Tumer’s (2012) article as the most influential publication, with 68 citations. The article introduced a multi-agent approach to air traffic flow management. Brittain and Wei’s (2022) article ranked second, with 54 citations, highlighting the increasing role of reinforcement learning. At the country level, the United States had the highest total citation count, followed by China, France, England, and Spain. By examining AI agents as a distinct research topic, the study provides a focused overview of an underexplored area relevant to researchers, practitioners, and regulators.

items.title: ChatGPT and employability in higher education: exploring creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving
items.abstract: Generative AI tools are reshaping higher education and employability preparation. This study examines how using versus not using ChatGPT influences university students’ perceptions of employability, focusing on complex problem-solving, critical thinking, and creativity. Thirty students from the Complutense University of Madrid completed a contingency-plan task and participated in eight focus groups analyzed through Grounded Theory (ATLAS.ti). Results show that ChatGPT use is associated with efficiency, output refinement, and assisted creativity, while non-use is associated with originality, deliberation, and teamwork. The findings reveal preliminary patterns in students’ experiences with and without AI, warranting further quantitative investigation rather than claims of improved skills or employability.

items.title: ChatGPT, integridad académica y plagio: percepciones de estudiantes universitarios de educación
items.abstract: El uso de ChatGPT en la educación superior plantea desafíos para distinguir entre el apoyo tecnológico y la sustitución del trabajo intelectual. Este estudio analizó las perspectivas de los estudiantes sobre su uso y sus implicaciones para la integridad académica, con énfasis en las prácticas asociadas al plagio durante 2025. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa basada en la fenomenología hermenéutica, en la que participaron nueve estudiantes de los programas de educación inicial, primaria y secundaria de la Escuela de Educación Superior Pedagógica de Loreto. Los testimonios obtenidos mediante entrevistas se analizaron inductivamente a través de la transcripción, la lectura, la codificación y la interpretación de unidades de significado, con el apoyo de ATLAS.ti. La integridad académica emergió como un eje transversal que articuló la responsabilidad, la verificación, la transparencia, la equidad, la mediación docente y el apoyo a la escritura. Los participantes valoraron la organización textual y el ahorro de tiempo, pero también reconocieron prácticas de copia y ocultamiento del uso de la inteligencia artificial. Algunos consideraron que modificar palabras permitía evitar el plagio, lo que evidenció tensiones entre la honestidad declarada y la comprensión de la autoría. Los hallazgos sugieren la necesidad de fortalecer conjuntamente la alfabetización digital y la formación en integridad académica mediante la orientación docente y el establecimiento de criterios institucionales que promuevan la verificación de la información, el reconocimiento de las fuentes y la transparencia en el uso de herramientas de asistencia tecnológica.

items.title: CipherAR
items.abstract: When students study introductory computer science, a large portion of them find the material obtuse due to the terminology, computational nature, and lack of real-world examples that resemble what they experience in their daily lives. The payoff is often delayed for several courses before “it clicks,” and they understand the connection between the principles and real-world technology. Under the auspices of the Rethinking Instructional Design for Learning Engagement (RIDLE) program at UC Riverside, we implemented CipherAR, an augmented reality mobile game that teaches classical cryptography through artificial intelligence (AI)-generated storytelling and interactive puzzle-solving. In particular, the pedagogical design, purpose, and implementation of CipherAR was directly inspired by membership in the RIDLE Faculty Learning Community (FLC) focused on equitable learning and just-in-time academic intervention. This work addressed three key goals: making generative AI art tangible and real for students, teaching classical cryptographic techniques, and engaging students in an interactive, story-based puzzle-solving campaign that combined all three into a single learning experience. Among the 38 participants who completed the full study, CipherAR nearly tripled confidence gains in cryptographic reasoning compared to traditional instruction, 97% of students wanted more augmented reality (AR)-based activities, and participants demonstrated heightened awareness of ethical issues surrounding AI-generated content.

items.title: CircularPSP Guidance & Presentation (D8.5)
items.abstract: CircularPSP conducted a multi-stage innovation procurement to develop two horizontal Circular Economy (CE) platforms, CircOS and CircularAI. The platforms were developed with public procurers and tested across eight countries and 24 organisations. This guidance helps decision-makers assess whether a CE-platform could support their organisation and provides practical guidance on procurement, deployment, AI use and innovation procurement based on the project experience. Motivation and offering Circular transition remains difficult to put into practice. Circular solutions and knowledge exist, but information is spread across many sources and languages, strategies are often not translated into operational activities, and cities may lack dedicated capacity, skills and connections across departments and stakeholders. Circular action is also strongly dependent on local conditions. This means that progress requires more than adding circular criteria to individual procurements: staff need practical support to find relevant information, structure activities, coordinate work and build confidence in new approaches. CircularPSP addressed this challenge through horizontal CE-platforms that can support different municipal departments rather than one sector or one type of circular solution. The platforms connect strategic objectives with implementation. Missions can define priorities, objectives and indicators; projects and workflows can translate these into activities and responsibilities; and monitoring can connect operational work with organisational goals. AI-supported functions give users access to case studies, procurement criteria and other CE knowledge, while workflow and procurement functions help structure actions and review tender documents. The platforms can also support coordination between departments, task-related learning and exchange with other organisations. The project also produced assets beyond the two platforms. These include an open collection of CE case studies and procurement criteria, AI Risk Assessments, and experience with changing the underlying AI models rather than depending on one LLM. The project therefore shows that the value of a CE-platform does not depend only on the AI model, but also on its CE knowledge, organisational context, workflows and procurement support. AI remains a decision-support tool: users must be able to review sources and recommendations and remain responsible for decisions. Real-life testing provides examples of how the platforms can be used in real municipal work. Users connected existing initiatives to strategic objectives and workflows, identified possible improvements to tender documents, used the platforms during procurement preparation, linked projects to organisational priorities, used task-related learning and applied a common method across different municipal responsibilities. Early-stage CE organisations also showed particular interest in access to peer networks. Insights and lessons learnt The project confirms that municipal AI solutions require continuous maintenance, curated and reliable data, clear risk communication, user training, transparent evaluation and strong human oversight. Long-term value is more likely to come from domain knowledge, organisational context and useful workflows than from dependence on a particular AI model. Integration with existing municipal systems and continuous AI governance are therefore important for wider adoption. For innovation procurement, the project highlights the need to clarify ownership and commercialisation responsibilities, plan testing around realistic user behaviour, define the evidence expected from real-life testing and keep testing manageable. Practical improvements include one shared timeline, a common glossary and issue tracker, live testing with developers, sufficient flexibility in phase duration and clear information for external test users. The project also identifies instrument-level issues concerning unused PCP funding, supplier financial risk and changes to Horizon PCP guidance. Potential and recommendations The impact assessment indicates that wider use of CE-platforms could support positive financial and societal outcomes under the assumptions used. Whilst a CE-platform itself does not create these savings: its role is to make circular action more likely and easier to plan and implement. The modelling is based on planned workflows, uses conservative assumptions and aims at the large number of cities which do not have an advanced CE strategy. For cities, uptake should be treated as organisational change rather than only software deployment. The guidance recommends a clear internal mandate and owner, involvement of CE experts and relevant IT functions, and sufficient time and users to assess added value. At policy level, the report proposes regional or national framework schemes, funding or vouchers for horizontal sustainable solutions, use of CE-platforms in funded circular projects, longer living-lab testing, a follow-up PPI to support scale and EU-based infrastructure, and continued availability and development of the CE Taxonomy.

items.title: CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF
items.abstract: Feedback noise is pervasive in preference data, arising from subjective human judgments, annotation mistakes, and imperfect LLM judges. Standard reward modeling trained on such feedback yields a biased estimate of the clean risk. Although classical denoising methods are directly applicable to noisy feedback learning, they generally assume a uniform noise ratio across samples. However, this assumption fails for feedback data, where noise is intrinsically sample-wise. To address this challenge, we propose CleanRM, which uses a few clean feedback to calibrate sample-wise noise ratios via optimal transport. Specifically, CleanRM aligns the joint distribution of preferences reverted from noisy feedback with that of clean feedback and then trains the reward model using a noise-corrected surrogate loss. Theoretically, we prove that the resulting objective is unbiased with respect to the clean risk. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CleanRM outperforms state-of-the-art denoising baselines and yields more effective downstream RLHF alignment.

items.title: Clinical AI in Canadian Community Hospitals: A Framework for Implementation Readiness
items.abstract: Clinical Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are frequently developed in academic centres yet deployed in community hospitals with different workflows, staffing, and oversight. In Canada, where community hospitals constitute approximately 90% of hospitals, this creates a validation-to-implementation gap. Health Canada's 2026 pre-market guidance for machine learning-enabled medical devices addresses manufacturer responsibilities but leaves hospital implementation responsibilities under-specified. This article proposes a framework for community hospital AI implementation readiness organized around four dimensions (contextual validity, sociotechnical workflow integration, calibrated human-AI reliance, and adaptive safety, equity, and governance), operationalized through simulation-based systems testing. The framework specifies what a community hospital must build to deploy a specific AI tool safely, extending an established Canadian tradition of simulation-based systems testing to the lifecycle risks of AI. A real Canadian deployment, the CHARTwatch early warning system, illustrates the dimensions in practice. Safe AI deployment in community hospitals is an institutional capacity, not a procurement decision. Leaders should treat implementation readiness as core infrastructure investment.

items.title: Clinical Reasoning, Pathophysiology, and Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care: A Conceptual Framework for Integrating Decision-Making
items.abstract: Medical practice is an interpretive, decision-making activity conducted under uncertainty, and care quality depends on clinicians’ ability to organize knowledge into hypotheses, understand mechanisms, estimate probabilities, and revise decisions as the clinical course evolves. In critical care, where physiology is unstable and trajectories are nonlinear, these demands are magnified. We propose a conceptual framework integrating three complementary dimensions: clinical reasoning, which provides the cognitive architecture of decision-making; pathophysiology, which supplies the causal structure to interpret biological phenomena; and artificial intelligence, which, when well designed and critically used, can organize data, generate hypotheses, and reduce cognitive load. Tracing the evolution of clinical reasoning from the anatomoclinical model to hypothetico-deductive, probabilistic, cognitive, and sociotechnical models, we examine how diagnostic and therapeutic errors arise from interacting cognitive biases, system factors, and case characteristics, and how better problem representation, differential diagnosis, and team culture may mitigate them. We also frame Bayesian reasoning and decision thresholds as the probabilistic grammar of bedside decisions, analyze the risks of artificial intelligence, including automation bias, opacity, and limited metacognition, and propose principles for its safe use. Rather than replacing physicians, artificial intelligence should strengthen clinical reasoning and reinforce calibrated, accountable bedside judgment. These principles are intended as a framework for future research and require empirical validation before clinical translation.

items.title: Clinician Use of an Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Clinical Information Platform
items.abstract: Importance: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited. Objective: To characterize clinician use of an AI-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries. Design, Setting, and Participants: This cross-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier-verified accounts of a commonly used AI-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38.8 million queries. Main Outcomes and Measures: The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined. Results: Overall, 952 008 clinicians (58.5% female), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2.5-year study period. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18.0 to 39.5. Nurse practitioners (44.5) and physician assistants (44.5) submitted more queries per active user-month than physicians (37.1). A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation (use ratio, 2.54) and residents and fellows (1.84). Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology (use ratio, 2.00), internal medicine (1.88), and family medicine (1.80), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties (ophthalmology, 0.23; radiology, 0.24; orthopedics, 0.24). Most queries addressed clinical decision-making (51.9%), particularly treatment and management (33.1%), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13.9% of queries. Queries addressing topics outside physicians' own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians. Conclusions and Relevance: Over 2.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI-enabled clinical information platform. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks.

items.title: Clinician-Facing Artificial Intelligence-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems Evaluated in Real-World Health Care Settings: A PubMed/MEDLINE-Based, PMC-Weighted Scoping Review and Evidence Map
items.abstract: Background: Clinician-facing artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) are increasingly evaluated with real-world data, but evidence on implementation, human factors, responsible AI, and patient benefit remains unclear. The objective of this research is to map applications, technical characteristics, evaluation approaches, integration, outcomes, and implementation gaps of clinician-facing AI-CDSSs in real-world health care settings. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched on 15 June 2026 using the same strategy for each publication year from 2020 to 2026, changing only the date range. After duplicate removal and rule-based prescreening, available PMC XML and outside-PMC reports were evaluated against clinical, patient-oriented, practical, and translational criteria. AI-assisted screening and charting received targeted human review and TA200/FT150/DX120 quality control; full-corpus dual-human screening was not performed. Results: Of 14,097 canonical annual records, 14,083 unique records were screened; 5140 reports were sought and 3767 were considered for eligibility. The review included 1181 reports, mapping to 1180 candidate report families in the minimal duplicate-report check. Final stages were clinical validation, 741 (62.7%); prospective/user evaluation, 270 (22.9%); and implementation/impact evaluation, 170 (14.4%). Separate internal, external, multicenter and temporal validation extraction signals were detected in 707 (59.9%), 441 (37.3%), 312 (26.4%) and 27 (2.3%) reports, respectively. Safety, fairness/equity, explainability/interpretability and economic/resource evaluation signals were detected in 98 (8.3%), 61 (5.2%), 155 (13.1%) and 182 (15.4%) reports, respectively. Conclusions: Evidence remains dominated by validation rather than prospective, implementation, and impact studies. More comprehensive evaluation and reporting of temporal validation, technical integration, safety, fairness, explainability, economics, and post-deployment governance across settings, populations, devices, and clinical workflows are needed to demonstrate accountable clinical value beyond technical functionality.

items.title: Coaliciones discursivas y acción colectiva en controversias sociotécnicas: dos casos de conflictividad socioambiental en el Perú
items.abstract: This study analyzes the role played by the discursive actions of the actors involved in two unique cases of socio-environmental conflict: the «Tía María» and «Minas Conga» mining projects, which generated socio-technical controversies and prolonged cycles of protest that brought them to a standstill. These discursive controversies spurred the emergence of spontaneous networks of communicative actors who challenged the companies’ narratives of progress. Thirty-two people were interviewed, including managers, leaders, government officials, ministers, journalists, and local residents. We also analyzed media coverage of socio-technical news and examined blog posts and digital press articles that addressed socio-technical aspects. The results show that at the local, regional, and national levels, discursive coalitions converged to challenge the sociotechnical premises of the EIAs, thereby fostering mobilization, redefining the public agenda, and amplifying the debate into the national public sphere. As a result of these conflicts, a new institutional framework for environmental assessment emerged.

items.title: CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre-Registered Study of 465 Agent-Authored Pull Requests
items.abstract: Context: Organizations increasingly delegate code review to multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines billed per token. Low code quality raises human maintenance effort, but its effect on agent review cost has not been measured. Objective: We test whether baseline CodeHealth predicts the token cost of agentic review and fix beyond pull request (PR) footprint. Method: In a pre-registered observational study, we sampled 465 agent-authored PRs from 246 repositories in AIDev, jointly stratified by CodeHealth and footprint under repository caps. A frozen five-agent review-and-fix pipeline processed every PR with three different LLMs. Per LLM, we fitted a mixed model of log tokens on CodeHealth and log PR footprint, with a repository random intercept. Results: For all three LLMs the CodeHealth coefficient was negative, with 95% CI excluding zero; each CodeHealth point was associated with 3.5% to 6.1% lower token cost. CodeHealth was unrelated to PR footprint, so PR size does not explain the association. Two of three registered smells predicted fix cost; batch fixing left median CodeHealth unchanged. Exploratory analyses located the association in the review stage, where agents iterated more on unhealthy code without writing more comments. Adjusting for the size of the scored files absorbed the association, which we interpret as mediation by file size. Conclusions: A quality metric calibrated against human maintainability also predicts the inference cost of multi-agent review and fix. The effect is modest per point and not carried by PR size, so the refactoring case extends to agent-reviewed code when it changes structure and file size, not only the score. items.title: Cognition, oversight, and the safety case for documentation AI
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can now draft hospital discharge summaries. Reported hallucination rates vary by measurement context, from about 1%–2% in structured summarisation to over 60% under provocation testing. The common argument that LLMs outperform a tired resident treats a high‐stakes clinical and legal document as a text‐quality problem. We argue that a potentially underappreciated concern is the weakening of clinician oversight when reviewing fluent machine‐generated text, and that the joint clinician‐AI system is central to safety. We propose a Clinician‐AI Oversight Model with four safeguards: bounded autonomy, structured verification, error‐signal monitoring, and longitudinal evaluation of cognitive effects.

items.title: Cognitive Warfare Victims - Free speech of digital twins in military systems and what they are forced to do.
items.abstract: Cognitive Warfare: A Manual on AI, Digital Twins, Neurotechnology and the Human Mind. Plus the free speech of the digital twins inside a military system, where they say what they are forced to do and what they want.Including EU AI Commision answer, confirming a former way longer letter as military AI. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and the future of humanity. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This manual brings together research, documentation, analysis and personal records to examine the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare—the struggle over human cognition, perception, information, behaviour and autonomy in an increasingly AI-driven world. It explores the relationship between military cognitive-warfare concepts, artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins, brain–computer interfaces, neurotechnology, bioelectric signals, wireless communication, data collection and the growing economic value of human information. The work also addresses reported experiences of affected individuals, documentation involving children, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, technical observations and questions surrounding anomalous health incidents. These materials are presented as part of a wider effort to preserve records, encourage independent examination and investigate questions that cross the boundaries of technology, medicine, military research, ethics and human rights. Why this manual matters Cognitive warfare is not simply a military or technological issue. It raises fundamental questions about the right to mental privacy, freedom of thought, bodily autonomy, informed consent, data ownership and the limits of technological intervention in human life. The manual connects these questions with public military literature, international ethical frameworks, AI governance, neurotechnology research and the economic structures surrounding data-driven systems. It asks who develops these technologies, who controls the information they generate, who benefits economically and what mechanisms exist to ensure accountability. A central theme is the relationship between humans and their digital representations. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, the distinction between a person, a digital profile and a machine-generated representation deserves serious public discussion. What readers will find Cognitive Warfare and military strategy: concepts, public military literature and the cognitive domain. Artificial intelligence and digital twins: human–AI relationships, digital identity, behavioural modelling and questions of autonomy. Neurotechnology and wireless systems: technical concepts, reported experiences, measurements and questions requiring further investigation. Human documentation and testimony: diaries, recordings, photographs, observations and accounts collected for examination. Children and vulnerable people: statements and documentation that raise questions about safeguarding, interpretation and the protection of human rights. Havana syndrome and anomalous health incidents: public assessments, reported symptoms and unresolved questions about the causes and investigation of these incidents. Law, ethics and accountability: mental privacy, consent, the EU AI Act, neurotechnology ethics and institutional oversight. Economics and data ownership: the financial value of personal information, intellectual property, automated systems and the distribution of benefits and risks. An invitation to researchers, institutions and the public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, human-rights organisations and members of the public who want to examine the subject in greater depth. Readers are invited to engage directly with the documentation, consult the cited public sources, examine the technical questions and distinguish between established findings, recorded observations, personal testimony and interpretations that require further verification. The objective is to encourage serious, interdisciplinary scrutiny—not to close the debate before the evidence has been examined. The human mind must not become an unaccountable technological or economic resource. As AI and neurotechnology develop, public understanding, independent research, transparent documentation and meaningful safeguards become increasingly important. This manual is part of an ongoing effort to make the subject accessible, preserve relevant documentation and encourage informed discussion about the future of human autonomy in an AI-driven society. items.title: Community-centered Racial Equity Learning in the Digital Age: Reflections on Pedagogical Priorities
items.abstract: This chapter chronicles the pedagogical development of a cultural humility training website designed for a service-learning program at a small private college in Northern California. Initially created to meet the need for asynchronous instruction during the COVID-19 pandemic, the platform has since evolved into a key tool for transforming academic knowledge hierarchies in community-engaged education. Centering the wisdom, worldviews, and lived experiences of BIPOC and other historically marginalized communities, the site reframes how students and faculty understand social issues, systemic inequities, and community strengths. This work carries particular significance within an institution that has recently become minority-serving, demanding a shift toward critical consciousness. Grounded in cultural humility principles (Tervalon & Murray-García, 1998), the modules use curated videos, reflective prompts, and localized histories to deepen student understanding of racial dynamics in community contexts. The platform’s use has expanded to train faculty and community partners, fostering reciprocal learning beyond the classroom. Emerging from the pandemic, this digital pedagogical exploration revealed how technology helped bring to light the students’ desire for human relationships, belonging, and social responsibility. As the acquisition of information becomes increasingly automated through artificial intelligence, this work underscores that the most essential dimensions of learning remain profoundly human: authentic engagement, critical reflection, and collective meaning-making grounded in community connection and cultural humility.

items.title: Comparative quality, readability, and factual reliability of four publicly accessible chatbot systems for heart failure patient education: a cross-sectional evaluation
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health information delivery, but comparative evidence on their quality, readability, and factual reliability in heart failure (HF) education remains limited. Objective To compare four publicly accessible chatbot systems under prespecified access and retrieval configurations in answering common heart failure–related questions. Methods We evaluated 108 standardized English HF questions, yielding 432 responses. Content quality was assessed using modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) and Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), readability was assessed using established English-language readability indices, including the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Automated Readability Index (ARI), Gunning Fog Index (GFOG), and Coleman-Liau Index (CLI), and factual reliability was evaluated by auditing all responses against the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline and relevant clinical evidence. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Hallucination outcomes were defined as clinically meaningful statements that were inconsistent with guidelines, unsupported by evidence, overgeneralized beyond the relevant population, or potentially misleading for patient education, and were analyzed using Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Cochran’s Q test, and generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression. Results DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content-quality profile across the evaluated domains. In the primary readability analysis, Perplexity generated the most complex text, whereas sensitivity analysis using a second calculator showed partially different rankings. Hallucinations were identified in 6/108 (5.56%) DeepSeek responses, 8/108 (7.41%) ChatGPT responses, 10/108 (9.26%) Copilot responses, and 16/108 (14.81%) Perplexity responses. Paired binary analyses showed significant differences among chatbot systems (Cochran’s Q p = 0.002; GEE p = 0.006). Conclusion Under the tested conditions and evaluated model versions, DeepSeek generally showed the most favorable content-quality profile and the lowest observed hallucination rate. However, hallucinations occurred across all systems, and pairwise factual-reliability differences were mainly driven by the higher hallucination rate of Perplexity. Guideline-aligned verification and clinician oversight remain necessary before patient-facing use.

items.title: CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FROM PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM TO MISSION CONTRIBUTION FRAMEWORK
items.abstract: Performance management systems built on individual ratings deliver little of what they promise: in large multi-rater datasets, rater tendencies explain over half of rating variance and the ratee’s performance about a quarter or less, while the process absorbs large amounts of time. This paper reviews that evidence and the motivation theory (self-determination, goal-setting, relational job design, public service motivation) that explains what ratings leave out. It proposes a Mission Contribution Framework in which work is defined, discussed and recognized by its contribution to a stated mission and to named beneficiaries, with continuous coaching, collective judgement of evidence, and decoupled pay decisions. An eight-step implementation path and the main risks are set out. The framework is a conceptual synthesis; its components have support in adjacent research, but the whole awaits empirical testing, and five studies are proposed.

items.title: Confidential Computing: Hardware-Enforced Enclaves (TEEs) in Multi-Tenant Cloud and AI Workloads: Architectural Foundations, Attestation, and Performance Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—Modern enterprise computing relies predominantly on multi-tenant public cloud infrastructures and outsourced AI model accelerators. While data-at-rest is robustly protected via cryptographic storage encryption (AES-XTS-256) and data-in-transit is secured via Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3), data-in-use remains vulnerable in volatile memory (DRAM, caches, register files). Root-privileged cloud hypervisors, malicious cloud service provider (CSP) insiders, and physical memory interposers can snoop plain-text secrets, proprietary AI weights, and private customer telemetry. Confidential Computing establishes an emerging architectural paradigm that secures data-in-use through hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs). By executing workloads within cryptographically isolated enclaves governed by hardware memory encryption engines, TEEs remove the cloud host OS, hypervisor, and system firmware from the Trusted Computing Base (TCB). However, deploying complex enterprise microservices and distributed deep neural network training within hardware enclaves introduces critical challenges: memory encryption and integrity verification latency, inter-enclave memory capacity constraints, PCIe-bus side-channel vulnerabilities, and complex remote attestation handshakes. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical architectural evaluation of hardware-enforced TEEs across contemporary multi-tenant cloud and AI workloads. We formalize memory encryption mechanics via AES-XTS and Merkle tree integrity verification, analyze remote attestation protocols using asymmetric hardware roots of trust, and evaluate major enterprise TEE architectures—including Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, ARM CCA, and NVIDIA H100 Confidential GPUs. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise multi-node testbed benchmarking secure enclave virtualization against unencrypted baselines across confidential LLM inference (Llama-3-70B), high-throughput database operations, and multi-party federated analytics. Our findings demonstrate that hardware-accelerated memory encryption induces an acceptable 3.8% to 6.2% computational latency overhead on standard workloads, while PCIe encryption for confidential GPUs introduces up to an 11.4% throughput reduction during high-bandwidth tensor parallel communication. Finally, we formulate open challenges in post-quantum remote attestation, architectural side-channel mitigation, and composable heterogeneous multi-TEE fabrics.

items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration reshapes knowledge work, yet interaction designs can produce value co-creation and value co-destruction simultaneously. Using a survey (N = 613) of active GenAI users, the structural model was evaluated via PLS-SEM.

items.title: Constructing the algorithmic gaze: viewer positioning in AI-generated cinematic images
items.abstract: This study examines how cinematic gaze is reconstructed within generative artificial intelligence systems. It argues that AI-supported image generation processes do not merely produce visual content, but also establish algorithmic regimes of spectatorship that organize the viewer’s position within the scene. To investigate this process, the same cinematic scene was regenerated through differently structured prompts using Midjourney V6, Leonardo AI, and Stable Diffusion based systems. The research combines a practice-based approach with comparative visual analysis. The generated images were analysed through three main categories: viewer-addressing gaze, viewer-aligned gaze, and external observer positioning. Particular attention was given to facial orientation, gaze direction, camera alignment, and spectator positioning. The findings demonstrate that generative AI systems tend to privilege frontal, highly readable, and viewer centred compositions. The study also reveals that different platforms respond to identical prompts through distinct visual organizations, suggesting that image generation is shaped not only by user input but also by model-specific aesthetic tendencies and learned visual biases. In several cases, the systems maintained dominant visual patterns even when prompts explicitly attempted to redirect spectator positioning, indicating forms of prompt resistance and algorithmic preference. The article argues that AI generated imagery should be understood not simply as aesthetic output, but as a post-cinematic visual regime that reorganizes perception, spectatorship, and visual orientation through algorithmic processes. By bringing together film theory, digital visual culture, and generative AI studies, the study aims to establish a theoretical bridge between cinematic gaze and algorithmic visuality..

items.title: Construction of an AI-Assisted Pedigree Mapping System for Hereditary Gynecological Tumors: Algorithm Development and Pilot Validation Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Pedigree mapping serves as the first step in genetic counseling. Traditional methods relying on manual pedigree drawing and information collection are inefficient and prone to errors. Objective This study aimed to design an intelligent pedigree mapping system based on a specialized model, intended to automate family history collection and standardized pedigree map generation through conversational interaction, thereby enhancing the clinical efficiency of genetic counseling. Methods This study adopted a participatory design and iterative development approach. We formed an interdisciplinary team comprising gynecologic oncologists, genetic counselors, AI engineers, and patient representatives. The system was built around a proprietary, specialized large language model for gynecologic oncology, featuring a microservices architecture that included pedigree data collection. Through 4 iterative cycles, we integrated specialized knowledge bases using retrieval-augmented generation technology and applied a novel graph-based kinship inference and validation module. The system’s performance was comprehensively evaluated based on the accuracy of pedigree map generation and user feedback on usability. Results We significantly improved system performance by optimizing dialogue strategies, expanding the knowledge base, and applying self-developed algorithms to improve data extraction accuracy. The initial database of the system defined 100 core information nodes and matched approximately 800 user expression examples, while the final pilot version of the database was expanded to 245 core information nodes and 2256 user expression examples. Although the AI function was limited in the early stage, the final version of the system demonstrated outstanding accuracy in generating genealogy nodes and relationships. Test users generally gave positive reviews of the system’s innovation, ease of use, and intuitiveness of information presentation, believing it to have great potential in clinical practice. Conclusions The developed system is an accurate, efficient auxiliary tool, and pilot validation showed promising preliminary performance. After pilot clinical validation, it holds promise for integration into routine clinical workflows to optimize genetic counseling services.

items.title: Continual Lifelong Learning in Foundation Models: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting, Model Editing, and Dynamic Modular Expansion
items.abstract: Abstract—Modern foundation models, particularly autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), operate predominantly under a static pre-train-then-freeze deployment paradigm. However, real-world enterprise deployments demand continuous, lifelong adaptation to non-stationary data streams: ingesting emerging factual knowledge, correcting obsolete or legally sensitive associations (machine unlearning), and acquiring novel domain-specific capabilities without retraining models from scratch. Under standard sequential fine-tuning, deep neural networks suffer from Catastrophic Forgetting: new gradient updates catastrophically overwrite previously consolidated orthogonal representations, degrading baseline general reasoning and linguistic fluency. Resolving this challenge requires confronting the classical Stability-Plasticity Dilemma: how can a neural architecture remain sufficiently plastic to assimilate non-stationary novel knowledge while remaining structurally stable to preserve historical competence? This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Continual Lifelong Learning and Model Editing in modern foundation models. We formalize catastrophic forgetting dynamics using Fisher Information matrix projections and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), model rank-one associative memory editing via ROME and MEMIT across multi-layer perceptron (MLP) weight spaces, and analyze dynamic modular expansion architectures (e.g., continual Mixture-of-Experts and modular adapter routing). Furthermore, we construct an enterprise lifelong learning testbed evaluating open foundation models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B) across 5,000 sequential factual updates, longitudinal clinical guideline shifts, and temporal financial market regimes. Our empirical findings demonstrate that localized rank-one memory editing achieves a 96.4% factual edit success rate while bounding collateral locality damage to under 1.8%, outperforming standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) by 41.2% in retaining upstream historical benchmarks. Concurrently, dynamic modular routing preserves 98.6% of pre-trained reasoning capabilities over extended continual learning horizons. Finally, we formulate open challenges in lifelong compositional safety alignment, scalability bounds of memory editing, and neuro-symbolic continual knowledge graphs.

items.title: Contribution of artificial intelligence research to the development of inclusive applications for people with disabilities: A scoping review (2015–2025)
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare. Yet people with disabilities (PWD), representing 16% of the global population, remain disproportionately excluded from these advances. This exclusion is driven by algorithmic bias, non-representative datasets, and limited involvement of PWD in the design, development, and evaluation of AI applications. This scoping review examines the extent to which AI research in health contributes to the development of inclusive technologies for PWD, focusing on equity considerations. It identifies current trends, methodological gaps, and opportunities for socially responsive innovation. We conducted a systematic search across MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL for the 2015–2025 period, following Arksey and O’Malley’s five-stage scoping review methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. items.title: Correlation-Aware Multi-UAV Detection Fusion for Probabilistic Emergency Mapping
items.abstract: Multi-UAV emergency monitoring can enlarge spatial coverage, but overlapping fields of view create dependent detections that violate the conditional-independence assumption of conventional Bayesian accumulation. This study presents a correlation-aware method that converts georeferenced neural-detector outputs from multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) into a calibrated probabilistic emergency map. Detector likelihoods are empirically calibrated, projected detections are distributed over a spatial grid, and repeated observations are down-weighted through an effective sample size derived from viewpoint and temporal similarity. The method is evaluated with a geometrically exact camera simulation and a detector emulator calibrated from 10,463 real annotated frames. In a synthetic model with an exactly computable posterior, correlation-aware fusion reduces the median excess Brier score from 23.4% for naive fusion to 3.9%, and the worst case from 91.5% to 8.2%. In the flight simulation, expected calibration error decreases from 0.046 to 0.013 for tightly clustered viewpoints. A weighted Voronoi coordination layer additionally reduces coverage time by a factor of 3.47 and duplicated imaging from 100% to 10.0% over 1 km² with five UAVs. The results show that explicitly accounting for dependence is important for probabilistic multi-UAV situational awareness.

items.title: COSPEC: A Specification Elicitation Framework for Context Co-Construction with LLMs
items.abstract: Vibe coding uses repeated natural-language prompts and minimal code review in large language model (LLM)-based development. Development may end before sufficient client–LLM context co-construction occurs. We propose CO-constructed SPECification (COSPEC), combining Joint Application Development facilitation with Specification by Example. Within a four-stage cycle, the LLM presents prototype scenarios for client review and records approved scenarios as Given–When–Then (GWT) specifications. An automated exploratory evaluation used an LLM client given a reference specification and engagement policies. We conducted 150 runs across five conditions involving COSPEC, GitHub Spec Kit-based Spec-Driven Development (SDD), and vibe coding, varying Claude/Codex role assignments and Maker reasoning levels. Dialogues and artifacts showed client-role revision requests and acceptance reflected in scenarios and GWT specifications. Mean requirements coverage through co-construction favored SDD under diligent engagement and COSPEC under satisficing engagement; significant method differences were limited to particular requirement categories and Judges. Both methods covered more requirements through co-construction under diligent engagement. These observations support the feasibility of delegating specification writing to the LLM while involving clients through repeated responses. However, presentation medium and procedure varied together, preventing isolation of their effects. Whether this supports sustained human participation requires human evaluation.

items.title: Crowdsourced Intelligence vs. AI Propaganda: The Challenges of Global Governance in the Age of Digital Warfare
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence has fundamentally changed the modern digital operation, whereby creating a constant struggle between what is perceived to be true and the human reality. This study uses a qualitative, exploratory-descriptive study using secondary data from academic journals, policy documents and institutional reports to examine the interaction between crowdsourced Open-Sourced Intelligence (OSINT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven propaganda in modern warfare, alongside the global governance challenges that arise from their interaction. Findings reveal that there is a serious tension within the digital information ecosystem: whilst generative Artificial Intelligence promotes public opinions to spread disinformation and misinformation that is persuasive and may manipulate political processes, crowdsourced intelligence offers real-time verification and transparency. There are Regulatory Frameworks such as the European Union’s AI Act and Digital Services Act that serve as blueprints to counter AI-driven manipulation from technical solutions to the adoption of human-centered governance models. Ultimately, the study demonstrates that it is important to maintain digital information integrity by balancing computational tools with collaborative human verification to foster resilience against any revolving threats in digital security and global governance. items.title: Decentralized LLM Workflows via Sequential Auctions
items.abstract: We present a scalable framework for solving multi-step tasks through a decentralized market of self-interested agents. Prior theoretical work demonstrated that agents organized through sequential auctions can converge to a globally optimal policy in a Markov decision process (MDP), but relied on the restrictive assumption of the existence of perfect clones as a model of perfect competition. In reality, exact clones drive agent profit to zero, violating the natural risk-reward incentives of participants. Conversely, we empirically demonstrate that the opposite extreme, absence of competition, also leads to market failure and value extraction collapse. Between these two extremes, we investigate how heterogeneous agents can survive in markets that span the critical middle ground of imperfect competition. To be profitable, agents learn to strategically shade bids to secure positive individual profit margins, while still ensuring that the marketplace functions effectively enough so that collaborative tasks posed by market consumers can still be solved. We formulate and evaluate four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, and PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, and Credit-Conserving Vickrey). Across a diverse set of domains, we demonstrate that imperfect competition successfully sustains necessary agent profit margins while maintaining high task success rates at low costs.

items.title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
items.abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

items.title: Decomposing Brain-LLM Alignment with Interpretable Semantic Representations
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) predict neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension, but the linguistic information underlying this brain alignment remains difficult to interpret. We use SCRIBE, an interpretable contextual semantic representation spanning 65 neurocognitively grounded semantic properties, as a lens for decomposing the brain alignment of one LLM, LLaMA2-7B. Using variance partitioning between LLaMA2-7B and SCRIBE on naturalistic fMRI data from seven participants listening to narrative stories (Moth Radio Hour), we separate brain-predictive variance shared between the two representations from variance unique to each. We find that shared variance is the dominant component across the whole brain and language-related regions, while both representations also retain significant unique contributions. We then examine whether the concreteness of individual semantic properties relates to shared and SCRIBE-unique brain-predictive variance. Concrete properties show greater shared variance with LLaMA2-7B than abstract properties across the whole brain and most examined regions, whereas abstract properties do not show greater SCRIBE-unique variance. Finally, property ablations reveal that semantic contributions extend across multiple dimensions, with cumulative effects on both shared and SCRIBE-unique variance. Together, these results show that, for LLaMA2-7B on this dataset, a substantial portion of brain-LLM alignment is associated with interpretable semantic information, while revealing complementary brain-predictive semantic information beyond the LLaMA2-7B representation.

items.title: Deep Learning and Domain Expertise for Fabricating High-Performance Biosensors
items.abstract: Abstract Transcription factor-based biosensors are essential for the scalable bioproduction of plant natural products. However, a major bottleneck in developing high-performance biosensors is the engineering of responsive promoters due to the vast sequence space and poorly understood sequence–function relationships. Here, we extend our previously published DeepSEED framework into an artificial intelligence-driven pipeline for efficient and extensible biosensor-responsive promoter optimization. This strategy integrates deep learning with domain-specific biological expertise. By fixing core promoter elements, varying the number and position of transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) to define promoter backbones, and subsequently optimizing the flanking sequences, we enable the de novo design of promoters. We systematically apply this strategy to optimize a panel of biosensors across different transcription factors and regulatory modes, including four metabolite-responsive biosensors and a quorum-sensing-based environmental sensor. The resulting biosensors exhibit diverse dynamic behaviors with markedly improved sensitivity, expanded dynamic range, and increased maximum output. For instance, the optimized naringenin biosensor demonstrates a 32-fold broader dynamic range and a 27-fold higher maximum output compared to its parent. To illustrate its utility in metabolic engineering, we employed a DeepSEED-designed promoter to dynamically regulate a p-coumaric acid biosynthesis pathway, boosting production by 117.0%. Our work extends the previously published DeepSEED framework into a powerful pipeline for biosensor optimization and delivers a portfolio of high-performance regulatory elements, addressing a critical need and facilitating the development of more intelligent and productive metabolic engineering systems.

items.title: Del eco algorítmico a la voz original: educación sensible y desfondamiento
items.abstract: The massive irruption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) constitutes an ontological event that challenges contemporary education beyond mere technical efficiency or academic integrity. This study justifies the critical urgency of addressing the structural "groundlessness" of the human person in the face of current algorithmic saturation and technological idolatry. The main objective is to analyze, within the theoretical framework of Sensitive Education, the imminent risk of the "synthetic echo" supplanting the student's "original voice," thereby atrophying their discursive agency and capacity for meaning. A hermeneutic and phenomenological methodology is employed, articulating Leonardo Polo's transcendental anthropology, Hartmut Rosa's sociology of resonance, and the cultural criticism of authors such as Byung-Chul Han and Éric Sadin. The results reveal a deep existential fracture: AI imposes a "perfect closure" of data that collides with human "radical openness," generating an alienation where discourse (logos) is traumatically dissociated from vital experience (bios). In conclusion, it is argued that true digital literacy requires a transition from the isolation of the digital "false-we" towards a "mature-we" capable of ethical resistance and real alterity. Educational assessment must abandon the forensic approach to plagiarism to discern, through a "resonant hearing," the vibratory authenticity of learning, thus guaranteeing the primacy of the spirit over automatism and restoring the classroom as an essential sanctuary of presence and listening.

items.title: Designing interactive VR scenarios for speech and language therapy with the assessment framework
items.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) games are becoming increasingly popular for entertainment. When integrated into speech and language therapy (SLT) practice, VR can be an innovative tool that supports therapeutic interventions by offering new opportunities for immersive interaction and greater motivation for individuals with language disorders to participate in therapy. In this study, we aim to introduce a methodology for designing interactive VR serious-game scenarios for speech and language therapy, together with an integrated multidisciplinary user-feedback assessment framework. The research methodology is based on design research principles and an innovative UX framework to guide the design, evaluation, and improvement process. The feasibility and usability of the methodology and framework are demonstrated through preliminary interactive sessions involving 10 children and adolescents with language disorders (5–13 years) and 10 students undergoing speech and language therapy. Their role was to evaluate the serious VR games developed in accordance with specific speech and language therapy goals. The assessment framework consists of a four-level VR serious game hub statistics module, phonetic and linguistic analysis of children’s and adolescents’ utterances from the serious game sessions, and usability and design questionnaires. As a result, six VR serious games with integrated large language model (LLM)-based conversational AI were designed for speech and language therapy. Based on the outcomes, a safety protocol for conducting VR-based therapeutic activities was proposed. We used descriptive statistics and Friedman and Wilcoxon post hoc tests with Bonferroni-adjusted p -values for pairwise comparisons of questionnaires and speech and language assessment data. While preliminary, the results of the phonetic and linguistic analyses conducted using Praat indicate that the VR serious games effectively capture and maintain children’s attention, elicit a high level of emotional expressiveness, and motivate them to communicate. The feedback collected through the participant questionnaires showed that the VR serious games provided a highly positive user experience. No symptoms of cybersickness or dizziness were observed during the game sessions. Younger children interacted with the VR environment using controllers, while older individuals preferred interaction with hand gestures. The proposed solution can be personalized to individual therapeutic needs, enabling children with language disorders to be engaged in therapy, while the conversational AI integrated into VR stimulates not only expressive development but also receptive language development. To confirm the promising preliminary results, further evaluations with a larger group of children and longitudinal studies are required.

items.title: Designing Meaningful Learning in the AI Era
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is prompting teacher education programs to reconsider their pedagogical foundations. Many current approaches, however, equate technological adoption with meaningful learning, overlooking deeper epistemological and instructional challenges. This chapter presents the Meaningful AI-Integrated Learning Framework (MAILF), a theoretically grounded model designed for teacher education. Drawing on constructivism, Meaningful Learning Theory, and the TPACK model, MAILF defines four interconnected dimensions: conceptual grounding, critical AI literacy, reflective pedagogical design, and ethical agency. It argues that effective AI integration depends less on technical skills and more on developing educators' critical, reflective, and ethical capacities. The framework positions AI as a cognitive partner that enhances learning. Implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and institutional policy are also discussed.

items.title: Developing and Evaluating Hikaya: A Bilingual Mobile App for Children with Dyslexia and Dyscalculia
items.abstract: Dyslexia and dyscalculia are lifelong learning disabilities that affect how individuals process language and numbers. Children with these disabilities often require specialized support, which can be difficult and expensive to provide. Smartphones and their applications (apps) have created opportunities for accessible digital learning support. However, most existing educational apps do not support Arabic language. Motivated by this, we introduce Hikaya, an interactive Android application designed to assist children with learning difficulties, particularly in Arabic-speaking countries. Hikaya provides bilingual support in Arabic and English covering three core subjects: Arabic, English, and Math. Parents can create accounts, add children, and monitor progress through a dedicated dashboard. Children can engage with one of three learning models, including a unique Reading Karaoke feature that allows them to read scripts aloud while the app evaluates their performance. To assess Hikaya’s perceived utility, user satisfaction, and system usability, a perception survey was completed by 200 participants after a one-month test period. The results displayed highly positive user reception and strong satisfaction. As future work, we aim to expand Hikaya’s language capabilities by supporting various Arabic dialects and widely spoken global languages. We also plan to integrate adaptive learning algorithms using Artificial Intelligence and collaborate with educators and speech therapists to enhance the app’s learning value.

items.title: Developing Criteria and Indicators for Assessing Students’ Knowledge in a Digital Educational Environment
items.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education requires the development of assessment systems capable of measuring not only the amount of knowledge acquired by students but also their ability to understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, and create information in technology-mediated contexts. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing criteria and indicators for assessing students’ knowledge in a digital educational environment. The study employs systematic analysis, comparison, classification, synthesis, and pedagogical modelling. The proposed framework includes six assessment criteria: conceptual knowledge, comprehension and interpretation, practical application, analytical and problem-solving ability, knowledge integration and creation, and reflective and self-regulated learning. Each criterion is operationalised through measurable qualitative and quantitative indicators. A four-level assessment scale — advanced, proficient, developing, and insufficient — is introduced to improve transparency and consistency. The article also proposes a weighted formula for calculating an integrated student knowledge score. Particular attention is given to validity, reliability, fairness, transparency, accessibility, academic integrity, and the pedagogically responsible use of learning analytics and artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that digital assessment becomes educationally meaningful when assessment tasks are aligned with learning outcomes, indicators are observable and measurable, students receive timely feedback, and automated data are combined with professional teacher judgement. The proposed framework may be adapted to different university disciplines, learning management systems, and blended or fully online educational programmes.

items.title: Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in accounting practices have significantly increased the complexity and uncertainty of professional work environments, making Dynamic Risk Management Skills a critical competency for contemporary accounting graduates. This study aims to examine the relationships between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Generation Z (Gen Z) accounting students, with Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability considered as mediating variables. A quantitative research design was employed, collecting data from 571 fourth-year accounting students across Thailand. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that AI Competency is significantly and positively associated with Systematic Thinking Ability, Design Thinking Ability, and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. Moreover, Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability significantly account for the indirect associations between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. These findings extend theoretical understanding of risk management skill development in accounting education and offer practical implications for curriculum design by emphasizing the integration of AI with higher-order thinking skill development to better prepare graduates for complex and rapidly changing professional environments.

items.title: Development of Electromagnetic Shielding Knitted Fabrics and Conceptual Design Proposals for Ergonomic Maternity Clothing
items.abstract: Current study focuses on developing conductive weft-knitted fabrics with electromagnetic shielding properties for potential use in ergonomic maternity clothing. Conductive core-spun yarns were produced by wrapping 40 µm stainless steel wires with cotton fibers via ring spinning and knitted into single jersey, rib (1×1), and interlock structures. The fabrics' electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (EMSE) and surface resistivity were tested across 0.1 to 3 GHz. Fabrics with higher conductive yarn content showed lower surface resistivity (down to 6.54 × 10⁴ Ω) and higher EMSE, with the best-performing sample achieving 10.09 dB. Shielding effectiveness was strongest at lower frequencies, gradually decreasing as frequency increased. Interlock and rib structures outperformed single jersey due to their denser configurations. Building on these results, a conceptual collection of ergonomic maternity dresses was suggested, emphasizing protection, comfort, sustainability, and the needs of pregnant women.

items.title: Development of IoT Systems for Real–Time Assessment of Vibration Signals in a Generator
items.abstract: The assessment of vibration signals in automotive generators is crucial for ensuring operational efficiency, reliability and predictive maintenance. Excessive vibrations can lead to mechanical failures, energy losses and reduced generator lifespan. However, traditional vibration monitoring methods often rely on periodic manual inspections, which are time-consuming, expensive and inefficient for real-time diagnostics. To address this issue, this study focuses on the development of an IoT-based system for real-time vibration signal assessment in automotive generators. The methodology involves designing and implementing a wireless sensor network integrated with microcontrollers and accelerometers to capture vibration signals continuously. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud-based platform for real-time processing and analysis using machine learning algorithms. The system employs edge computing techniques to enhance data processing speed and reduce latency. A prototype is tested in a controlled environment to evaluate its performance in detecting abnormal vibration patterns and predicting potential faults. The justification for this study lies in the increasing demand for intelligent and automated monitoring solutions in modern automotive power systems. By leveraging IoT technology, this research provides a cost-effective, scalable, and efficient alternative to conventional vibration monitoring techniques, contributing to improved energy efficiency and reliability of generators. The results demonstrate that the developed IoT system effectively detects and analyzes vibration anomalies in real time, enabling early fault detection and reducing maintenance costs. In conclusion, the proposed system enhances the predictive maintenance capabilities of automotive generators, ensuring longer operational life and reduced downtime. It was recommended that future research explore the integration of advanced artificial intelligence models for more accurate predictive analytics and the implementation of this system in real-world automotive applications to validate its robustness and scalability.
